messages:
julia: quick design check-in — proposal to split the egress operator into two clear surfaces: a Control API (hosted control plane) and an Agent API (runs in customer VPC). goal: minimize control-plane trust, enable customer-managed networking + fixed-egress-ip options, and reduce blast radius on private deployments. looking for tradeoffs we missed.

sanjay: SGTM as a high-level idea. main concern: contract for IP preservation and SNAT behavior. if agent runs in-customer we need explicit lifecycle for EIP/BGP registration + clear semantics for source IPs.

maria: curious about latency/fastpath — adding an agent handshake to CP could add RTT for cold-starts. can we keep a local fastpath for KV cache and batching so token-per-token latency doesn't regress?

julia: agreed. sketching approach: long-lived mTLS bidi stream for control + separate local unix socket for runtime fastpath. control plane only pushes config + model routing decisions. agent keeps KV cache and does prefix caching locally. proto sketch below.

julia: ```proto
syntax = "proto3";
service EgressAgent {
  rpc OpenControl(stream ControlMsg) returns (stream ControlMsg);
  rpc RegisterEgress(RegisterReq) returns (RegisterRes);
}
message ControlMsg {
  oneof payload { ConfigDelta delta = 1; Heartbeat hb = 2; }
}
```

kevin: security note: private deployments can't call our KMS/HSM. we need a token + key-wrap model so agent never has cleartext persistent keys. also require cert rotation endpoint and audit events for egress mapping changes.

ops-oncall: runbook questions: how do we emergency-kill an agent if it's leaking traffic? need a reversible step (eg patch to denylist) and quick re-route back to hosted egress. also need metrics to detect surges.

sanjay: for fixed-eip customers we should support two modes: 1) operator-managed EIP (we program NAT/route) and 2) customer-ads EIP (customer advertises via BGP or shares a static mapping). expose this in RegisterEgress + webhook for lifecycle events.

maria: also who enforces per-tenant rate-limiting and batching? if agent is in-customer we still need to prevent noisy neighbors. proposal: control plane issues scoped tokens with quotas; agent enforces local rate caps and reports counters.

julia: nice. i'll add quota tokens to the API contract. migration plan idea: canary 5% tenants on dedicated agents, compare P50/P95 token latency and cost delta, fallback to hosted model if regressions.

devops-bot: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/4587 (egress-operator-api-contract) :white_check_mark:

sanjay: include network partition tests: simulate flaky control link, delayed config, and ensure agent backoff is jittered. verify no global state corruption on reconnect.

kevin: security checklist draft: mTLS mutual auth, minimum TLS1.3, mutual cert rotation (30d), signed attestation of agent binary, audit log stream to control-plane-only, and limited admin RPCs over a separate channel.

ops-oncall: emergency kubectl snippet for private deployments (for runbook):

ops-oncall: ```bash
# cordon node running agent
kubectl label node agent-node-123 drained=true
# patch agent to deny egress mapping
kubectl patch deployment egress-agent -n infra --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-","value":{"name":"AGENT_MODE","value":"DENY_EGRESS"}}]'
```

julia: action items: (1) i'll open the API spec PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4612), (2) @sanjay please draft EIP/BGP lifecycle flow, (3) @kevin produce security checklist + tests, (4) @ops-oncall draft runbook + rollback playbook. sync tomorrow 10:00am in #architecture. :thumbsup:

maria: +1, i'll add perf benchmarks and a small harness to measure local batching impact.

sanjay: +1. i'll also add a small terraform example for customers to register an EIP.

julia: thanks all — will tag folks on the PR when it's ready.
